bull_bear.body:
- Robust technical expertise and customer-centric innovation, cited by management as the basis of competitive advantage
- Integrated manufacturing infrastructure following the demerger, enabling integrated operations across the specialty surfactants segment
- Dedicated, fully operational R&D centre at Koparkhairane, Navi Mumbai, supporting co-development and accelerated product validation with major domestic and international customers
- Diversified product portfolio of 50+ products spanning surfactants, blends, mild surfactants, pearlising agents and preservatives
- Long-standing partnerships with leading FMCG and industrial clients; customer base of 100+ and technical support accessibility cited within its competitive advantages
- Switching friction from customised, application-specific formulations co-developed with customers and validated against their regulatory standards
- Supply-chain diversification and sourcing flexibility for critical raw materials, with long-term procurement relationships reducing resource concentration
- Breadth of end-market reach — 50+ countries and seven named end-use industries — limiting dependence on any single application
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Margin compression in a low-margin specialty surfactants business — The company describes EBITDA margin of 5.51% and net profit margin of 1.48% for FY26 in its own overview, down from 7.56% and 2.27% respectively in FY25 even as revenue grew 30.35% — growth is coming without commensurate profitability, so any further input-cost or pricing pressure bears directly on a thin margin.
- Narrow manufacturing footprint — only two facilities — The Corporate Overview discloses a manufacturing network of just 2 facilities (plus one R&D centre in Navi Mumbai). Concentration in so few sites makes operations exposed to any single-site disruption.
- Customer concentration in a B2B FMCG-supplier model — The company states a customer base of 100+ customers and a vision to be the 'Global Partner of Choice for leading FMCG companies'. A B2B book of this size serving large FMCG buyers concentrates bargaining power with a small number of counterparties.
- Regulatory and compliance exposure on product formulations — The company says it develops customised formulations addressing 'evolving performance, regulatory and sustainability requirements', and lists 'Strengthen Regulatory Compliance' as one of its stated strategic priorities — regulatory change in home and personal care ingredients is a standing structural exposure.
- Leverage and finance-cost burden — Finance costs rose to ₹1,230.53 lakhs in FY26 from ₹1,155.15 lakhs in FY25 per the Board's Report summary, absorbing a large share of profit before finance costs and tax — a fixed charge that compounds the thin operating margin.
- Subsidiary drag on consolidated earnings — Consolidated profit for FY26 (₹1,234.21 lakhs) is lower than standalone (₹1,267.83 lakhs) in the Board's Report summary, and the 2026 milestone describes the Company as consolidating and strengthening operations across its existing and subsidiary entities — the subsidiary is a drag rather than a contributor.
- Export / international-market exposure across 50+ countries — The company reports global reach across 50+ countries and a vision of being the global partner of choice for leading FMCG companies; a footprint of this spread carries foreign-exchange and cross-border demand exposure that the report does not quantify in this material.
- Frontier and business-entity risks flagged at the Risk Management Committee — The Board's Report records that familiarisation programmes covered 'Economic Environment & Global Scenario, Frontier Risks, Business Entity Risks, etc. at the Risk Management Committee Meetings', and states that managing risk is a strategic priority underpinned by a framework to identify potential threats and ensure operational continuity — management explicitly treats these as live watch-items, though the report text does not enumerate them further.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: ASL manufactures specialty surfactants, blends, mild surfactants, pearlising agents and preservatives used as ingredients in cleansing, emulsification, dispersion and performance-enhancement formulations. It sells to home care, personal care, beauty and wellness, oral care, baby care, agrochemical and industrial customers in India and international markets, developing customised formulations that address evolving performance, regulatory and sustainability requirements. Its stated competitive advantage rests on technical expertise, customer-centric innovation, a diversified product portfolio, integrated manufacturing infrastructure and dedicated R&D facilities, alongside long-standing partnerships with leading FMCG and industrial clients.

outlook.body:
- Maintain focus on business performance while adapting to market developments in a dynamic operating environment shaped by the broader economy and the personal care and surfactants industry
- Serve a diversified portfolio of surfactants and specialty products, which management credits for the healthy demand recorded during FY 2026
- Manage pricing alignment and order patterns through changing customer procurement and inventory behaviour, including the effects of GST-related pricing dynamics on certain end-use industries
- Manage raw-material exposure to Fatty Alcohol and Fatty Acids, which continued to account for the majority of the Company's raw material purchases
- Keep the Board constituted for effective strategic guidance, with an optimal balance of Executive and Non-Executive Directors including Independent Woman Director(s), and a Board of Eight Directors as on March 31, 2026
- Sustain leadership continuity — the Board has recommended the re-appointment of the CEO & Managing Director and an Executive Director each for five years with effect from August 20, 2027, and the appointment of an additional Non-Executive Independent Director from August 22, 2026
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: This material carries no capex or expansion narrative: no plant, line or capacity-addition project, no commissioning, ramp-up or debottlenecking timeline, and no project cost is described. The only footprint facts stated are that the Company operates 2 manufacturing facilities and 1 advanced Research & Development Centre in Navi Mumbai, and that among its eight stated strategic priorities are to Expand High-Value Specialty Products and Expand Global Presence — stated priorities, not projects. The 2026 milestone in 'Our Journey' is Business Consolidation, described as continuing to focus on consolidating and strengthening business operations across its existing and subsidiary entities with emphasis on operational efficiencies, resource optimisation, financial discipline and sustainable growth; the 2025 milestone records that a fully operational R&D Centre was established. The Board's annual evaluation criteria include 'investment / Capex' among the matters on which information flow to the Board is assessed, but no capex programme is disclosed.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Management says that during FY 2026 the Company recorded strong business growth, with healthy demand across its diversified portfolio of surfactants and specialty products, revenue from operations rising 30.4% to ₹859.13 crores from ₹659.09 crores
- Management describes the operating environment as dynamic, with evolving customer requirements, changing demand patterns and external market uncertainties
- GST-related pricing dynamics influenced pricing alignment and purchasing patterns across certain end-use industries, causing variations in buying behaviour and order patterns during parts of the year — a management-attributed driver
- Supply-side conditions remained structurally tight and volatile, with fatty alcohol prices elevated on feedstock constraints, capacity dynamics and geopolitical disruptions; oleochemical prices stayed firm as PKO production fell short of expectations
- A brief Q3 price correction, supported by record palm oil output and inventory build-up, proved short-lived; prices firmed again on seasonal Southeast Asian supply tightness, front-loaded restocking and Middle East tensions raising freight, insurance and logistics costs
- Petrochemical feedstocks were relatively stable for most of the year but came under sharper cost pressure towards the end of the period amid supply disruptions, input availability constraints and elevated crude oil prices
- Management expects crude oil markets to remain volatile and relatively elevated in 2026, citing IMF (April 2026 WEO) base-case average of around $82/bbl and World Bank (April 2026 Commodity Markets Outlook) of approximately $86/bbl, with significant upside risks on prolonged supply disruption and moderation over the medium term
- Management states the raw material supply environment is expected to remain dynamic, with feedstock availability, crude oil prices, logistics constraints and geopolitical developments continuing to influence input costs and pricing
- Industry context cited by management: the global surfactants market is valued at USD 47.4 billion in CY 2025 and projected to grow at a 5.4% CAGR between CY 2026 and CY 2033, with bio-based surfactant demand projected to outpace legacy synthetic alternatives and Asia-Pacific (particularly India and China) expected to lead volume growth
- India's surfactants market is cited at USD 3,186.5 million in CY 2025 (about 6.7% of the global industry), projected to reach USD 5,156.8 million by 2027 at a 6.2% CAGR, with bio-based surfactants the fastest-growing segment; rising urbanisation and organised retail are named as the volume drivers across homecare and personal care
- Macro backdrop cited: India's real GDP growth of 7.7% in FY 2026, projected at approximately 6.6% for FY 2026-27 with CPI inflation projected at 5.1%; India's chemical manufacturing sector described as contributing 7% to national GDP and expanding at a stable 2.8% CAGR
- Management flags geopolitical developments and global energy price volatility as key risks for India given energy import dependence, noting West Asia tensions raised crude prices and could pressure the merchandise trade balance
- Financial-ratio movements management attributes: inventory turnover rose 25.11% on account of increase in sales during the year; debt-equity ratio fell 20.86% and return on networth declined 12.67%
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Aarti Surfactants Limited is a specialty surfactants and ingredients manufacturer supplying home care, personal care and industrial formulators across 50+ countries, created in 2018 by the demerger of Aarti Industries' home and personal care division.

open.item: Management flags that GST-related pricing dynamics influenced pricing alignment and purchasing patterns across certain end-use industries, with customer procurement and inventory decisions producing variations in buying behaviour and order patterns during parts of the year.

The Company discloses an estimated amount of contracts remaining to be executed on capital account and not provided for (net of advances) as at 31st March, 2026, lower than the prior-year comparative — but the disclosure block prints no unit, so the quantum is not usable.
The Board recommended a dividend of Re. 1.00 per share (10%) for FY 2025-2026 subject to shareholder approval at the ensuing 8th AGM, resulting in a stated total payout.

The Board has recommended for member approval at the 8th AGM the re-appointment of Mr. Nikhil P. Desai as CEO & Managing Director and Mr. Santosh M. Kakade as Executive Director, each for five years with effect from August 20, 2027, and the appointment of Prof. Vandana B. Patravale as Non-Executive Independent Director for five years with effect from August 22, 2026.

Management expects crude oil markets to remain volatile and relatively elevated in 2026, citing third-party base-case averages of around $82 per barrel (IMF April 2026 WEO) and approximately $86 per barrel (World Bank April 2026 Commodity Markets Outlook), with significant upside risks in the event of prolonged or severe supply disruptions — a cited external projection, not company guidance.
Management lists expanding high-value specialty products as one of eight stated strategic priorities.
Management lists expanding global presence as a stated strategic priority, consistent with its vision of becoming the global partner of choice for leading FMCG companies.
Management lists accelerating R&D-driven innovation as a stated strategic priority; the R&D facility at Koparkhairane has been established and is expected to accelerate product validation.

Management lists driving digital process improvements and enhancing operational efficiency among its stated strategic priorities, and says it is committed to leveraging technology, modern digital tools and process digitization to improve risk responsiveness and process efficiency.
Aarti HPC Limited, the wholly owned subsidiary acquired in December 2019, remains yet to commence operations as on March 31, 2026 — a trackable status item, not yet an outcome.

Management flags that the raw material supply environment is expected to remain dynamic, with feedstock availability, crude oil prices, logistics constraints and geopolitical developments continuing to influence input costs and pricing.

For 2026 the Company says it continues to focus on consolidating and strengthening its business operations across its existing and subsidiary entities, with emphasis on operational efficiencies, resource optimisation, financial discipline and sustainable growth.

risks.risk: Margin compression in a low-margin specialty surfactants business
risks.note: The company describes EBITDA margin of 5.51% and net profit margin of 1.48% for FY26 in its own overview, down from 7.56% and 2.27% respectively in FY25 even as revenue grew 30.35% — growth is coming without commensurate profitability, so any further input-cost or pricing pressure bears directly on a thin margin.

risks.risk: Narrow manufacturing footprint — only two facilities
risks.note: The Corporate Overview discloses a manufacturing network of just 2 facilities (plus one R&D centre in Navi Mumbai). Concentration in so few sites makes operations exposed to any single-site disruption.

risks.risk: Customer concentration in a B2B FMCG-supplier model
risks.note: The company states a customer base of 100+ customers and a vision to be the 'Global Partner of Choice for leading FMCG companies'. A B2B book of this size serving large FMCG buyers concentrates bargaining power with a small number of counterparties.

risks.risk: Regulatory and compliance exposure on product formulations
risks.note: The company says it develops customised formulations addressing 'evolving performance, regulatory and sustainability requirements', and lists 'Strengthen Regulatory Compliance' as one of its stated strategic priorities — regulatory change in home and personal care ingredients is a standing structural exposure.

Finance costs rose to ₹1,230.53 lakhs in FY26 from ₹1,155.15 lakhs in FY25 per the Board's Report summary, absorbing a large share of profit before finance costs and tax — a fixed charge that compounds the thin operating margin.

Consolidated profit for FY26 (₹1,234.21 lakhs) is lower than standalone (₹1,267.83 lakhs) in the Board's Report summary, and the 2026 milestone describes the Company as consolidating and strengthening operations across its existing and subsidiary entities — the subsidiary is a drag rather than a contributor.

The company reports global reach across 50+ countries and a vision of being the global partner of choice for leading FMCG companies; a footprint of this spread carries foreign-exchange and cross-border demand exposure that the report does not quantify in this material.

risks.risk: Frontier and business-entity risks flagged at the Risk Management Committee
risks.note: The Board's Report records that familiarisation programmes covered 'Economic Environment & Global Scenario, Frontier Risks, Business Entity Risks, etc. at the Risk Management Committee Meetings', and states that managing risk is a strategic priority underpinned by a framework to identify potential threats and ensure operational continuity — management explicitly treats these as live watch-items, though the report text does not enumerate them further.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Aarti Surfactants Limited is a specialty surfactants and ingredients manufacturer supplying home care, personal care and industrial formulators across 50+ countries, created in 2018 by the demerger of Aarti Industries' home and personal care division.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: ASL manufactures specialty surfactants, blends, mild surfactants, pearlising agents and preservatives used as ingredients in cleansing, emulsification, dispersion and performance-enhancement formulations. It sells to home care, personal care, beauty and wellness, oral care, baby care, agrochemical and industrial customers in India and international markets, developing customised formulations that address evolving performance, regulatory and sustainability requirements. Its stated competitive advantage rests on technical expertise, customer-centric innovation, a diversified product portfolio, integrated manufacturing infrastructure and dedicated R&D facilities, alongside long-standing partnerships with leading FMCG and industrial clients.

group_structure.title: Group structure (subsidiaries / JV / related parties)
group_structure.body:
- Aarti HPC Limited — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary (100% subsidiary), CIN U24290MP2019PLC085837, acquired December 26, 2019 pursuant to Section 2(87)(ii); yet to commence operations. Not a material subsidiary (net worth/turnover does not exceed 10% of consolidated net worth/turnover). Investment made in it during the year.
- Aarti Industries Limited — related party: Controlling individuals / KMP influence; the Company's home and personal care division was demerged from it. Reimbursement of expenses transactions during the year.
- Aarti USA Inc. — related party: Controlling individuals / KMP influence; sale of goods (net of returns) during the year.
- Aarti Drugs Limited — related party: Controlling individuals / KMP influence; purchase of goods during the year.
- Valiant Organics Limited — related party: Controlling individuals / KMP influence; purchase of goods during the year.
- Aarti Pharmalabs Limited — related party: Controlling Individuals / KMP influence; purchase of goods during the year.
- Aarti Surfactants Limited Employees Group Gratuity Scheme — related party: Post Employment Benefit Trust; received contribution and dividend during the year.
- Mr. Rashesh Gogri — related party: Promoter Group; rent paid to him during the year.
- Ms. Priyanka Chaurasia — related party: Company Secretary (ICSI M.No: A44258) — Key Management Personnel.
- Mr. Nitesh Medh — related party: Chief Financial Officer (ICAI M.No: 155868) — Key Management Personnel.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Specialty ingredients:** Surfactants, Blends, Mild Surfactants, Pearlising Agents, Preservatives
- **Home Care end-applications:** Dishwashing Liquids, Detergents, Surface and Floor Cleaners, Hand Washes
- **Personal Care end-applications:** Body Washes, Shampoos, Moisturisers, Lotions

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Home Care
- Personal Care
- Beauty & Wellness
- Hair Care
- Oral Care
- Baby Care
- Agrochemicals
- Industrial Applications (textiles, coatings, manufacturing)
- India — domestic sales 82% of FY 2025-2026 geographical sales split
- International markets — 18% of FY 2025-2026 geographical sales split, across 50+ countries

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Management says that during FY 2026 the Company recorded strong business growth, with healthy demand across its diversified portfolio of surfactants and specialty products, revenue from operations rising 30.4% to ₹859.13 crores from ₹659.09 crores
- Management describes the operating environment as dynamic, with evolving customer requirements, changing demand patterns and external market uncertainties
- GST-related pricing dynamics influenced pricing alignment and purchasing patterns across certain end-use industries, causing variations in buying behaviour and order patterns during parts of the year — a management-attributed driver
- Supply-side conditions remained structurally tight and volatile, with fatty alcohol prices elevated on feedstock constraints, capacity dynamics and geopolitical disruptions; oleochemical prices stayed firm as PKO production fell short of expectations
- A brief Q3 price correction, supported by record palm oil output and inventory build-up, proved short-lived; prices firmed again on seasonal Southeast Asian supply tightness, front-loaded restocking and Middle East tensions raising freight, insurance and logistics costs
- Petrochemical feedstocks were relatively stable for most of the year but came under sharper cost pressure towards the end of the period amid supply disruptions, input availability constraints and elevated crude oil prices
- Management expects crude oil markets to remain volatile and relatively elevated in 2026, citing IMF (April 2026 WEO) base-case average of around $82/bbl and World Bank (April 2026 Commodity Markets Outlook) of approximately $86/bbl, with significant upside risks on prolonged supply disruption and moderation over the medium term
- Management states the raw material supply environment is expected to remain dynamic, with feedstock availability, crude oil prices, logistics constraints and geopolitical developments continuing to influence input costs and pricing
- Industry context cited by management: the global surfactants market is valued at USD 47.4 billion in CY 2025 and projected to grow at a 5.4% CAGR between CY 2026 and CY 2033, with bio-based surfactant demand projected to outpace legacy synthetic alternatives and Asia-Pacific (particularly India and China) expected to lead volume growth
- India's surfactants market is cited at USD 3,186.5 million in CY 2025 (about 6.7% of the global industry), projected to reach USD 5,156.8 million by 2027 at a 6.2% CAGR, with bio-based surfactants the fastest-growing segment; rising urbanisation and organised retail are named as the volume drivers across homecare and personal care
- Macro backdrop cited: India's real GDP growth of 7.7% in FY 2026, projected at approximately 6.6% for FY 2026-27 with CPI inflation projected at 5.1%; India's chemical manufacturing sector described as contributing 7% to national GDP and expanding at a stable 2.8% CAGR
- Management flags geopolitical developments and global energy price volatility as key risks for India given energy import dependence, noting West Asia tensions raised crude prices and could pressure the merchandise trade balance
- Financial-ratio movements management attributes: inventory turnover rose 25.11% on account of increase in sales during the year; debt-equity ratio fell 20.86% and return on networth declined 12.67%

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Maintain focus on business performance while adapting to market developments in a dynamic operating environment shaped by the broader economy and the personal care and surfactants industry
- Serve a diversified portfolio of surfactants and specialty products, which management credits for the healthy demand recorded during FY 2026
- Manage pricing alignment and order patterns through changing customer procurement and inventory behaviour, including the effects of GST-related pricing dynamics on certain end-use industries
- Manage raw-material exposure to Fatty Alcohol and Fatty Acids, which continued to account for the majority of the Company's raw material purchases
- Keep the Board constituted for effective strategic guidance, with an optimal balance of Executive and Non-Executive Directors including Independent Woman Director(s), and a Board of Eight Directors as on March 31, 2026
- Sustain leadership continuity — the Board has recommended the re-appointment of the CEO & Managing Director and an Executive Director each for five years with effect from August 20, 2027, and the appointment of an additional Non-Executive Independent Director from August 22, 2026

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: This material carries no capex or expansion narrative: no plant, line or capacity-addition project, no commissioning, ramp-up or debottlenecking timeline, and no project cost is described. The only footprint facts stated are that the Company operates 2 manufacturing facilities and 1 advanced Research & Development Centre in Navi Mumbai, and that among its eight stated strategic priorities are to Expand High-Value Specialty Products and Expand Global Presence — stated priorities, not projects. The 2026 milestone in 'Our Journey' is Business Consolidation, described as continuing to focus on consolidating and strengthening business operations across its existing and subsidiary entities with emphasis on operational efficiencies, resource optimisation, financial discipline and sustainable growth; the 2025 milestone records that a fully operational R&D Centre was established. The Board's annual evaluation criteria include 'investment / Capex' among the matters on which information flow to the Board is assessed, but no capex programme is disclosed.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Robust technical expertise and customer-centric innovation, cited by management as the basis of competitive advantage
- Integrated manufacturing infrastructure following the demerger, enabling integrated operations across the specialty surfactants segment
- Dedicated, fully operational R&D centre at Koparkhairane, Navi Mumbai, supporting co-development and accelerated product validation with major domestic and international customers
- Diversified product portfolio of 50+ products spanning surfactants, blends, mild surfactants, pearlising agents and preservatives
- Long-standing partnerships with leading FMCG and industrial clients; customer base of 100+ and technical support accessibility cited within its competitive advantages
- Switching friction from customised, application-specific formulations co-developed with customers and validated against their regulatory standards
- Supply-chain diversification and sourcing flexibility for critical raw materials, with long-term procurement relationships reducing resource concentration
- Breadth of end-market reach — 50+ countries and seven named end-use industries — limiting dependence on any single application
